rows.chunks: # Dew heater guide Dew forms on the secondary mirror when the mirror cools below the dew point. On Gull Point this happens on most nights between September and April. ## Procedure 1. Plug the heater strap into port DH-2 on the controller, never DH-1, which is reserved for the finder scope. 2. Set the controller to 40 percent output at the start of the session. 3. If the humidity reading passes 85 percent, raise the output to 70 percent. 4. Switch the heater off before closing the dome so the strap does not cook the baffle tube. ## Part numbers The replacement heater strap is part ZX-4471. The controller's spare fuse is part ZX-0090, a 2-amp slow-blow fuse.

Public meteor night # Public meteor night Each August the co-op opens Gull Point to the public for the Perseids. Visitors park in the lower lot and walk up; no cars are allowed past the gate after 21:00. Volunteers hand out red-light torches at the gate. White lights, including phone screens, are not allowed on the observing field.

Night log template  Record the following at the start of every session: observer name, booking block, sky transparency on a scale of 1 to 5, seeing estimate in arcseconds, and the dome temperature.  At the end of the session record the number of frames taken, any faults, and whether the dew heater was used. Faults must also be reported in the co-op chat within 24 hours.

Tidewater Telescope Co-op - Member Handbook   1. Membership   The Tidewater Telescope Co-op is a volunteer-run observatory on Gull Point. Annual membership costs 85 dollars for adults and 30 dollars for students. Members receive a key card for the dome and may book the main instrument after completing the orientation course.   The orientation course runs on the first Saturday of every month and takes about three hours. It covers dome safety, the mount controls, and the dew heater procedure.2. The main instrument   The main instrument is a 16-inch Ritchey-Chretien reflector on an equatorial fork mount. Its focal ratio is f/8 and the native focal length is 3250 millimetres. The camera is a cooled monochrome sensor that must be cooled to minus 10 degrees Celsius before any science frames are taken.   Never slew the mount while the dome shutter is closed below 40 degrees altitude; the tube can strike the shutter lip. The emergency stop is the red button on the north pier.3. Booking and data   Bookings are made in two-hour blocks, at most three blocks per member per week. A booking is released automatically if the member has not badged into the dome within 30 minutes of the block start.   All raw frames are copied each morning to the co-op archive and kept for 18 months. Members who want their data kept longer must export it themselves before it expires.
Winter closure notice, 2025  The dome was closed from 20 December 2025 to 5 January 2026 for the annual mount service. No bookings were accepted during the closure.
